title: Ryan T. Dobson
text:
The short version

I am a Ph.D. student in the Evolution and Society area of the Department of Psychology at the University of New Mexico. My research focuses on the evolutionary and developmental foundations of human social relationships and sexual behavior. Much of my work examines cross-sex friendships, relationship dynamics, and the developmental pathways that shape variation in sexual behavior.
I am broadly interested in integrating multiple methodological approaches—including genetically informed designs, longitudinal and intensive longitudinal data, and hormonal measures—to better understand how biological and environmental processes jointly influence human social and mating behavior.

title: Ryan T. Dobson
text:
What I work on

Three threads run through my work. Each one asks how biological and environmental processes jointly shape human social and mating behavior.



01

Cross-sex friendship and courtship
How mating motivations shape friendships between men and women, and how courtship behavior is signalled and perceived within them.

Mating psychology Relationships




02

Hormones and the ovulatory cycle
How women’s sexual psychology and emotional states shift across the cycle, and what estradiol and progesterone have to do with it.

Intensive longitudinal Endocrinology




03

Sexual development and behavior genetics
Using genetically informed designs to separate environmental effects from genetic confounding in how families shape sexual development.

Adoption designs Sibling comparison

pub_cors_all()
pub_cors_all() quickly generates a publication-ready correlation table for a set of variables.

#grab specific variable names as a vector
ll_aos <- names(ll[, grepl("rec_aos", colnames(ll))])

#create a vector to display names nicely (optional)
nice_names <- c(
  "oral sex"        = "rec_aos_pt_1",
  "pleasing sexual" = "rec_aos_pt_2"
)

pub_cors_all(data       = ll, #dataset
             cor_vars   = ll_aos,  #vector of variabl names from the dataset to include in analysis
             rename_vec = nice_names, #named vector to map new variable names
             cor_use    = "pairwise", #defaults to "pairwise" deletion of cases
             rnd        = 2 #default rounds to 2
             )

pub_cors_by()
pub_cors_by() is an extension of pub_cors_all() that takes a dichotomous grouping variable and displays correlations for one group above the diagonal, and the other below.
I have updates to this function that I haven’t incorporated into my package yet which includes:

automatic calculation of the difference between grouping variable calculations (helps quickly identify interaction effects in correlations)
easier argument specification so as automatically specify group levels based on the grouping variable provided


pub_cors_by(data        = ll, #dataset
            cor_vars    = ll_aos,  #vector of variabl names from the dataset to include in analysis
            group_var   = "sex_bio",
            groups      = levels(ll$sex_bio),
            rename_vec  = nice_names, #named vector to map new variable names
            cor_use     = "pairwise", #defaults to "pairwise" deletion of cases
            rnd         = 2 #default rounds to 2
             )

mlm_groupmean()
mlm_groupmean() is a function that helps to easily decompose variables into within- and between-group variance. This is a really handy function if you do any multilevel model analyses.

ll2 <- ll |> pivot_longer(cols      = c(rec_g_1, ex_g_1),
                              names_to  = "love_form",
                              values_to = "gift_1")
  mlm_groupmean(ll2,
              variables     = "gift_1",
              group         = "pid",
              within_affix  = "within_person_",
              between_affix = "between_person_",
              affix_type    = "prefix", #add a prefix. 'suffix' is the other option
              include_z     = TRUE #includes Z-scored versions of the variables
              ) |>
  select(matches("pid|gift_1|within_|between_")) |>
  arrange(pid) |>
  head()
